newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices continue down, yield gap widens.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices continue down, yield gap widens.

text.p: Danish bond prices continued their undramatic downward trek on Friday in the wake of Wall Street declines, with dealers seeing little change ahead in the general trend and pointing to a possible further widening of the 10-year yield gap with Germany.
"A widening of the bond differential to over 70 points cannot be written off. Otherwise little change is expected although foreign investors seem cautious," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.10 point down from the start at 110.56, yielding 6.41 percent in turnover of 2.4 billion crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's March future fell 0.34 point to 110.60 with 290 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.40 point to 89.10.
The crown traded at 3.8158 per mark at 1220 gmt, down a tad from around 3.8150 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 68.
